Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family holiday is approaching, which is a traditional time for everyone to reconnect.
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Story: The clock read 11:47 p.m. when my phone buzzed. I was already thinking about the upcoming family holiday, making mental lists of dishes to prepare and calls to make—my children and grandchildren expected me to keep everyone connected, especially during these special times. But now, my friend’s name flashed on the screen. I answered, and her sobs filled the quiet house. She’d just lost her brother, and her pain was raw, desperate. She needed me to listen, to be present, to offer comfort. Yet, in the back of my mind, I worried about being tired tomorrow, about missing the early morning call with my daughter to finalize holiday plans. My family counted on me to be the glue, to keep traditions alive. But my friend needed me now, in this moment, more than ever. I felt torn, my heart pulled in two directions, unsure how to be both the grandmother my family expected and the friend my heart wanted to be.
